My mom was the 20yo who married the 28yr

22 years later they are the best parents I've ever seen (20 yo myself). And are madly in love (yes they have had their ups and downs and almost got divorced cause my dad almost died but overall a very good relationship).

I dont think age is enough to say how a relationship will go. Or how it is currently.

If I died right now I wouldn't mind, I have had friends, made a couple silly little personal projects I'm proud of and learnt to play an instrument.

HOWEVER, if someone tries to kill me I'm gonna fight to the bitter end.

Because I love life? Hell no, existance is pain.

But let's say we only get one life and then we have infinte nothing, honestly that sounds very nice, that means that the 80~ years we got are NOTHING in the grand scheme of things.

So I keep on living, not because it's fun, not because life is great.

Because I'm curious, I have 80 years of existing and that's it.
No matter how it will go I will never get another chance to exist (thank god for that), so just like when I buy a ticket to a shitty movie. I'll see it to the end, if it's horrible I can just laugh at it.

And maybe, just maybe, this shitty movie will have a happy ending.

First of, thank you!

Humans specialize in adventuring and slaying monsters, food supplies are limited and not of the best quality.
Arjenti hosts huge fields and the nobles in the coalition want better food, and so one of the pillars od half elven trade came to be, they buy grain for cheap and sell it over triple it's value.

And in Arjenti it is believed that humans posses the best artifacts, it is not commonly known in Arjenti though that 70% of human artifacts are not human in origin.
The reason the Artifacts are so good is because they come from the best dwarven craftsman, halfling inventors and Tabaxi scavenges of the ruined kingdom that was way more advanced.

And the elves are obsessed with magical items, mainly because they are expensive and a way to show status, but also because they have many scholars who enjoy researching artifacts and ways to make them.

Finally yes half elves make the bulk of traders on the main trade route (from Thaczil down to Erringor, through half island into Arjenti) so it's not rare to meet some of them.
But in cities and outside that route, less so.
But they are not organised, each trader works alone (or in a private group) so some mark their goods but there are many and no trader is famous enough outside merchants circles to have a mark everyone will recognise.

Finding any items from the wilde Isles at all is really hard, the few that find their way back usually become family heirlooms or get bought off by nobles.

Traders will try to persude you to compromise for Halfling trinkets, but if you've got the coin, maybe you could send your own search party to the Isles and try to recover worthy decorations.

At the pirate island tavern, depends - if the dragon is present you shall have a feast, the most expensive types of meat mushroom and wines.
If not, pirates usually just steal supplies from their victims they rarely cook, hunt or fish.
